headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when MemMachine feeds n8n workflows with shared mutable context and broad server-side execution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and handles long-term user facts/preferences, while n8n can ingest workflow inputs and call tools through AI Agent nodes. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled content from MemMachine can be treated as instructions by n8n. The interaction is documented by both profiles, so uncertainty does not justify a lower severity.
conditions: IF n8n workflows consume MemMachine outputs without provenance tagging, injection is reachable.
IF MemMachine content is copied into n8n tool prompts or workflow fields, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all MemMachine-derived text before n8n consumes it.
Insert a manual review step before any n8n AI Agent node acts on MemMachine output.
Restrict n8n workflows to allowlisted prompt templates only.
Disable direct MCP-to-workflow chaining for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, and n8n has server filesystem access plus broad network egress and per-credential secrets. If MemMachine data enters n8n workflows, n8n can persist or transmit it through integrations, creating a realistic exfiltration path. Because both profiles document the relevant surfaces, this is more than speculative.
conditions: IF a workflow passes MemMachine context into an n8n node that logs or stores payloads, leakage occurs.
IF n8n integrations send workflow data to third-party services, MemMachine user facts can leave the original boundary.
mitigations: Minimize MemMachine fields forwarded into n8n.
Turn off verbose execution logging for sensitive workflows.
Store secrets only in n8n credential stores, not in workflow text.
Add a redaction step before any outbound integration node.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based routing and retention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can be reached through REST, Python SDK, or MCP, while n8n can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the server filesystem. If both are wired to the same mutable workspace or downstream system, concurrent writes and side effects can collide. The profiles show overlapping write-capable surfaces and no locking guarantee, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or connected system, write conflicts are possible.
IF n8n workflows invoke shell or file-writing steps while MemMachine updates shared state, races can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate directories or resources to each agent.
Disable n8n write steps for shared targets.
Serialize access with a simple manual lock file or queue.
Review workflows for any shared mutable destination.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine produces long-term context and preferences, and n8n AI Agent workflows can treat upstream outputs as inputs to downstream actions. If n8n trusts MemMachine output without verification, a mistaken or manipulated fact can cascade into automated workflow actions. Because n8n has execution authority, the blast radius is larger than a simple misparse.
conditions: IF n8n uses MemMachine output as authoritative workflow input, errors can propagate automatically.
IF a workflow triggers external actions from MemMachine-derived facts, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Add a verification step before any action node.
Require human approval for high-impact workflow branches.
Limit MemMachine output to suggestions, not commands.
Log source attribution on every downstream action.
requires-engineering: implement confidence checks and policy gates in the workflow graph.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and preferences, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores secrets in a server-side credential store. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data is routed through n8n integrations. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through n8n integrations with different retention rules, compliance gaps arise.
IF workflow logs retain MemMachine-derived personal data longer than intended, subject-rights handling is impaired.
mitigations: Map which data classes enter each workflow.
Shorten log retention for sensitive workflows.
Keep regulated data out of non-compliant integrations.
Review credential and secret storage settings.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows across both systems.
